phrases_language: English. The UK has no foreign language to learn: English is what you will be spoken to in. These sixteen entries are everyday British vocabulary that visitors from other English-speaking countries and non-native speakers actually run into (queue, loo, lift, chips and so on), not a foreign language. The 'English' column gives the standard international wording and the other column the usual British equivalent. They are editorial, compiled for this guide, not from a cited official source; no government body publishes a list of British usage. Welsh, Scottish Gaelic and Irish are also official or recognised languages in parts of the UK, but none was researched here and all visitors can use English throughout.

timezone_note: America/New_York is the Eastern zone — the one most visitors land in — but the country is not on one clock. The mainland spans four zones (Eastern America/New_York, Central America/Chicago, Mountain America/Denver, Pacific America/Los_Angeles), plus Alaska (America/Anchorage) and Hawaii (Pacific/Honolulu): six zones, and nine hours between Eastern and Hawaii in summer. Per NIST, daylight saving time runs 8 March to 1 November in 2026, beginning and ending at 2:00 a.m. local time (second Sunday of March to first Sunday of November); the IANA tz database agrees, putting America/New_York on EDT (UTC-4) today and switching it to EST (UTC-5) at 02:00 on 1 November 2026. NIST states DST is not observed in Hawaii, American Samoa, Guam, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, or the state of Arizona (except the Navajo Nation, which does observe it) — so Arizona is on America/Phoenix (UTC-7 year-round) and is an hour off its neighbours for half the year. Book domestic connections against the local zone, not a single national offset.
passport_validity_rule: U.S. Customs and Border Protection requires visitors to hold a passport valid for six months beyond the intended period of stay in the United States. Citizens of the countries on CBP's published exemption list (the 'six-month club') are exempt from that rule and need only a passport valid for their intended period of stay — the list is long and includes most of Europe, the UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, India, Brazil, Mexico and Singapore. CBP's Carrier Liaison Program publishes the current list; the edition current for this guide is dated 18 December 2025 and supersedes all earlier Carrier Liaison Program bulletins.
entry_requirement_notes: Entry is either visa-free under the Visa Waiver Program with an approved ESTA, or on a visa — and which one applies depends on nationality, not on the trip. CBP states the VWP covers citizens of 42 participating countries for tourism or business stays of up to 90 days; everyone else needs a visa from a U.S. embassy or consulate. VWP travellers must hold an e-Passport (CBP FAQ). ESTA must be approved before travel (air, sea or land), and CBP states an approval is typically valid for two years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first. ESTA fee, in force today: DHS's fiscal year 2027 inflation notice (Federal Register, 1 October 2026) sets it at $40.62 per travel authorization ($17 + $10.62 + $13), and CBP began assessing that amount on 16 October 2026; it was $40.27 before that date. If the application is denied only the $10.62 cost-recovery component is charged. The same notice leaves the HR-1 Form I-94 fee at $24 and sets the EVUS enrollment fee at $31.75 (EVUS applies only to People's Republic of China nationals holding certain U.S. visas, not to other travellers). Visa integrity fee: HR-1 created a $250 fee on nonimmigrant visas, but the only official text found says DHS would implement it in a future publication, and no implementation notice was found; collection was not confirmed as in force today (travel.state.gov sits behind a human-verification check and was not read), so check the State Department fee page if you need a visa. Entry restriction in force today: a CDC order (continued on 11 October 2026 for 30 days) bars entry of foreign nationals who were in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda or South Sudan within the previous 21 days. Global Affairs Canada also notes a U.S. proclamation, in force since 1 January 2026, restricting entry for certain nationalities, and that officers may search electronic devices. Apply for ESTA only through CBP's official ESTA channels (esta.cbp.dhs.gov); third-party sites charge a markup. Onward ticket: 8 CFR 217.2(c)(1) requires VWP applicants arriving by air or sea to hold, at the time of arrival, a round-trip ticket carrying them out of the United States to a foreign port or place (a ticket terminating in contiguous territory or an adjacent island counts only if the traveller is a resident there). The same regulation says a round-trip ticket is NOT required of VWP applicants arriving at a land border port of entry, who must instead show the CBP officer evidence of financial solvency and a domicile abroad they intend to return to. CBP is explicit that an approved ESTA does not guarantee entry: admissibility is decided by the CBP officer on arrival. Cash: anyone entering or leaving with more than $10,000 in currency or monetary instruments (combined for family or group travellers) must report it to CBP, on FinCEN Form 105; carrying more is legal, failing to report is not.

health.notes: No vaccination is required to enter the United States as a short-term visitor. The one that was — proof of COVID-19 vaccination for non-citizen, non-immigrant air passengers — ended at 12:01 a.m. EDT on 12 May 2023, when the underlying presidential proclamation was revoked; the State Department's notice records that change. Not stated here: CDC's Travelers' Health destination pages exist for travellers leaving the United States, not arriving in it, so there is no official CDC recommended-vaccination list or malaria-risk statement for the USA as a destination to cite here. (Separate, stricter vaccination requirements apply to immigrant visa applicants and adjustment of status, not to tourists.) Separate from vaccination: a CDC order currently suspends entry of foreign nationals who were physically present in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda or South Sudan in the past 21 days (Ebola); the order was last continued on 11 October 2026 for 30 days. Global Affairs Canada's U.S. advice (updated 15 October 2026) confirms proof of vaccination, including yellow fever, is not required for entry.

emergency.notes: 911 is the single number for police, fire and emergency medical services anywhere in the United States — there is no separate number per service. The call reaches a local Public Safety Answering Point, which dispatches the right agency. Do not plan on 112: FCC consumer guidance states that 112 is an international/EU number and does not work in the United States, and that 911 is what you dial here. Sourcing caveat, stated plainly: fcc.gov returns 403 to automated retrieval, so the 112 point was read from search results quoting the FCC's own page rather than fetched first-hand; the safe instruction either way is dial 911.

getting_around.summary: There is no single national transport pass and distances are continental — most visitors fly between regions and get around locally by car or rental car. Amtrak is the national intercity passenger rail operator; its USA Rail Pass covers 10 segments over 30 days to more than 500 destinations in Coach class for $499, with the pass usable within 120 days of purchase and the 30-day clock starting on the first segment. Amtrak's separate California Rail Pass is no longer sold to new customers as of 26 August 2026, though passes already bought are still honoured. For anyone visiting federal parkland, the America the Beautiful annual pass is the one broadly worthwhile national pass. Practical framing (not from a cited source): outside the Northeast Corridor, rail is a scenic option rather than a fast one, and much of the West is difficult to reach without a car.

passes.name: America the Beautiful — National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Annual Pass
passes.covers: Entrance fees and standard amenity (day-use) fees at federal recreation sites run by the National Park Service, U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, U.S. Forest Service, Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Reclamation and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. Covers either one private vehicle fee or four per-person fees, depending on how the site charges. Valid one year from purchase.
passes.worth_it: $80 for U.S. residents, $250 for non-residents (NPS pricing as published, page last updated 5 January 2026). Only worth it if you will enter several fee-charging federal sites within the year — entrance fees vary site by site, so check the specific parks on your route before buying. Senior options are cheaper: $20 annual, $80 lifetime.

passes.name: Amtrak USA Rail Pass
passes.covers: 10 rides (segments) over 30 days, Coach class, to a choice of more than 500 destinations on the Amtrak network.
passes.worth_it: $499, which Amtrak frames as under $50 per segment — so it pays only if you actually use long, expensive legs rather than short hops. The pass is valid for 120 days from purchase, but once you start the first segment you have 30 days to finish the rest. Reservations are still required per segment.

timezone_note: Uzbekistan's government portal for foreigners (my.gov.uz) lists the time zone as UTC+5, which agrees with the IANA zone Asia/Tashkent (UTC+5, no daylight saving time). The national hydrometeorological service Uzhydromet supplies the Tashkent forecast and climate data to the WMO.
passport_validity_rule: Official sources disagree, so the stricter reading is recorded: the passport should be valid for at least 6 months from the date you enter. Uzbekistan's government portal for foreigners (my.gov.uz/en/for-foreigners) says 'Your passport needs at least six months' validity from entry', and Global Affairs Canada says 'at least 6 months from the date you enter Uzbekistan'. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa page (gov.uz/en/mfa, last updated 2025-03-06) words it for visa applicants as at least 6 months from the date the visa is issued, and elsewhere asks for validity 3 months longer than the visa. The UK FCDO says the passport must expire at least 3 months after arrival, and the Uzbekistan tourism board's older travel guide (labelled 'Travel Information 2020') says 3 months beyond the visa's validity. No official source reconciles the 3-month and 6-month versions, so carry a passport with 6 months left to avoid being refused at check-in or at the border. The passport must also be in good condition; entry is refused with an invalid travel document or a passport reported lost or stolen (FCDO, Global Affairs Canada).
entry_requirement_notes: VISA: Uzbekistan's government portal for foreigners (my.gov.uz/en/for-foreigners) says visa-free stays depend on nationality: no time limit for Azerbaijan, Georgia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia and Ukraine; up to 60 days for the Kyrgyz Republic; up to 30 days for many countries including the US, UK, Germany, France, Japan, Korea, Turkiye and Canada; and up to 7 days for China including Hong Kong. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa page (gov.uz/en/mfa, last updated 2025-03-06) still lists a 10-day regime for China, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman with a flight ticket to the home or a third country, and does not yet list the US among the 30-day countries; the Tourism Committee on gov.uz (published 2025-11-03) says Presidential Decree No. 203 lets US citizens enter visa-free for up to 30 days from 1 January 2026. The 30-day period starts when you cross the border and you must leave when it ends (MFA page). The UK FCDO states visits of up to 30 days for tourism or business do not need a visa and advises asking for an entry stamp because exit checks rely on it. Other nationalities can apply for an e-visa at e-visa.gov.uz, the official portal; my.gov.uz says it needs a valid passport, a digital photo and the consular fee, processing usually takes 2 to 5 working days, and a single-entry e-visa covers up to 30 days (up to 60 in some cases). The MFA page lists e-visa fees of USD 20 single-entry, USD 35 double-entry and USD 50 multiple-entry (both up to 30 days) as of its 2025-03-06 update. Check the current list for your passport on e-visa.gov.uz or with an Uzbek embassy: India is not named in any of the visa-free lists read here. REGISTRATION OF FOREIGNERS: this is a real requirement and official sources give slightly different wording. my.gov.uz says to register your place of stay within three working days of arrival; hotels and similar accommodation register guests automatically (through the E-mehmon system); with a private host the host registers you via my.gov.uz or at the local internal affairs office; you are exempt if transiting or staying no more than three working days; re-register within three days if you move; keep the registration document because it may be checked at exit border control; violations can bring a warning or fine and serious or repeated ones a shortened stay or deportation. The older government portal page (oldmy.gov.uz/en/tourism) says three days from arrival excluding Sundays and holidays, with children under 16 not subject to temporary registration. The UK FCDO says weekends count towards the 3 days, that you must register again if you move city and stay more than 3 days, that campers must register themselves on E-mehmon within 3 days and pay a daily tourist tax online, and that missing or late registration can bring daily fines and possible deportation; Global Affairs Canada says stays longer than three days require registration and to keep the slip. Because the weekend rule differs, plan on registering within three calendar days and keep every hotel registration slip. CUSTOMS AND CURRENCY: foreign cash may be brought in without a limit but must be declared; Global Affairs Canada says to declare foreign currency worth more than USD 2,000, the Uzbekistan tourism board's older guide (labelled 2020) says the same threshold, while the UK FCDO says to declare cash over USD 10,000. The thresholds disagree and Uzbekistan's State Customs Committee pages could not be read (customs.uz returned only a title, old.customs.uz did not resolve), so declare any foreign cash above USD 2,000 to be safe. The FCDO says to complete two copies of the customs declaration, have both stamped, and keep one for exit, and that you cannot leave with more foreign currency than you declared. Precious metals or gemstones over 65 grams must be declared (FCDO). MEDICINES AND OTHER: carry a doctor's prescription and declare prescription medicines on the customs form; the FCDO warns that some UK over-the-counter medicines such as codeine can cause problems and that drones are largely prohibited without an import licence and permission. Global Affairs Canada says some areas, including parts of the Surkhandarya region, need special permission from the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Carry photo ID at all times; the FCDO says police often check and failing to carry it can mean a fine or arrest. Uzbekistan does not recognise dual nationality. Whether an onward ticket is required for visa-free visitors is not stated by any source read (the MFA page requires a ticket only for the 10-day regime countries), so it is recorded as unconfirmed; carry a return booking anyway. Blank-page requirements are not stated by any source read.

Hepatitis A
Hepatitis B

COVID-19

health.notes: The US CDC's Uzbekistan page (last reviewed 25 August 2026) says yellow fever vaccine is not required for country entry and not recommended, and Global Affairs Canada says proof of yellow fever vaccination is not required. The CDC page has no malaria section and the UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada pages do not mention malaria, so malaria risk is left unstated rather than guessed; check TravelHealthPro. CDC recommends hepatitis A, hepatitis B, MMR, COVID-19 and routine vaccines, says to consider typhoid, says rabies-infected dogs are commonly found and that rabies vaccine for exposures may only be available in larger urban facilities, and lists Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever among non-vaccine-preventable risks; Global Affairs Canada says the Crimean-Congo risk is generally low for most travellers and advises tick-bite precautions. The UK FCDO says medical care is generally poor, hospitals can be badly equipped, insurers usually refer serious cases to hospitals in Europe or New Delhi, there is no reciprocal healthcare agreement with the UK, and you should have insurance covering local treatment and medical evacuation; it also says outdoor air quality is poor from November to February, mainly in Tashkent and the Fergana valley, and often poor all year in Karakalpakstan and Khorezm. Global Affairs Canada warns counterfeit or expired medicines are common and that some prescriptions may be unavailable. Importing medicines needs a prescription and declaration (FCDO) and, per the tourism board, Ministry of Health permission. Uzbekistan's Ministry of Health website (gov.uz/ssv) was opened but publishes no travel-health or entry vaccination page for visitors.

money.card_acceptance: The UK FCDO says credit cards are not widely accepted outside Tashkent and other main cities, and ATMs accepting international cards are scarce outside major cities; travellers' cheques are generally not accepted. The tourism board's older guide (labelled 'Travel Information 2020') says international cards are mainly accepted at large restaurants and hotels, with shops, catering places and local transport usually taking cash in so'm.
money.cash_culture: The FCDO says US dollars are the most easily exchanged foreign currency, to exchange only at official booths because black-market exchange is illegal with harsh penalties, and that booths reject damaged or marked notes and US dollars issued before 2013. Global Affairs Canada also says buying money on the black market is illegal. Carry enough cash for regions outside the main cities.
money.atm_notes: The FCDO advises withdrawing cash in a main city before travelling to regions, because ATMs accepting international cards are scarce outside major cities. The tourism board's older guide (labelled 2020) says Visa and Mastercard can be used at ATMs in airports, hotels and tourist sites. No official source consulted states ATM fees or dynamic-currency-conversion practice, so none is stated.

emergency.notes: Uzbekistan's government portal for foreigners (my.gov.uz/en/for-foreigners) lists 112 as the 'SOS Emergency Line', and the UK FCDO says a unified emergency number, 112, was introduced in 2024 for all emergency calls and that the older numbers still work (police 102, ambulance 103, fire 101). The Uzbekistan tourism board's travel tips page and Global Affairs Canada list only the older numbers (fire 101, police 102, ambulance 103), and the tourism board adds gas emergency 104; if 112 does not connect, use those. The Unified Safe Tourism Call Center is 1173 (my.gov.uz, tourism board); the FCDO says it is open 24/7 and its operators speak English, Uzbek and Russian. The tourism board says a tourist police force exists to help visitors but gives no separate number, so tourist_police is left null. An older tourism board page (labelled 2020) lists a 'general emergency' number 1050, which no other source consulted confirms, so it is not used. The FCDO says its page does not list a tourist police unit.

getting_around.summary: Per the official tourism board, the Afrosiyob high-speed train serves routes such as Tashkent to Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva, the Tashkent Metro is open daily from 06:00 to 00:00, city buses cost 1,700 so'm per trip (paid on board) and intercity buses run daily with tickets sold at avtoticket.uz; its figures are undated, so check current fares and times. Yandex Taxi and MyTaxi apps work in Tashkent and Samarkand (tourism board), and the UK FCDO advises using licensed taxis such as official airport taxis or app-booked cars, notes many taxis lack rear seatbelts, and says you need your passport and a valid visa to book train tickets. Free Wi-Fi is available on the Tashkent Metro (my.gov.uz). The tourism board lists Uzbekistan Airways flights from more than 50 cities. Traffic drives on the right; the FCDO says a UK licence is valid for 30 days together with a 1968 international driving permit obtained before travel.

connectivity.local_sim_notes: Uzbekistan's government portal for foreigners names Beeline, Uzmobile and Mobiuz as tourist SIM providers. The tourism board's older guide (labelled 'Travel Information 2020') says foreign citizens need a passport and proof of temporary residence (such as hotel registration) to connect a number and that SIMs are sold at Tashkent and Bukhara airports and in operator offices in cities; it is undated for current rules, so whether registration is still required is not confirmed. No official source states eSIM support.

phrases_language: Uzbek (Latin script, the official script; Russian is widely used and English is used for international communication per the tourism board)

timezone_note: One offset nationwide, all year. The IANA time zone database splits the country into Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (south Vietnam) and Asia/Bangkok (north Vietnam), but both are UTC+7 and neither observes daylight saving, so the distinction never changes a traveller's clock.
passport_validity_rule: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the date you arrive in Vietnam, must carry at least 2 blank pages, and must be undamaged — travellers have been refused entry and exit over passport damage. You must enter and leave Vietnam on the same passport. Sourced from the UK FCDO's Vietnam entry requirements because Vietnam's own portals (evisa.gov.vn, xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn, travel.state.gov) refused automated access; Vietnam's national tourism authority separately states an e-visa applicant's passport must be valid 'for at least 6 months more'.
entry_requirement_notes: From 15 April 2026 all foreign nationals arriving at Tan Son Nhat Airport (SGN), Ho Chi Minh City are encouraged, not yet required, by the Vietnamese government to complete a digital arrival card online before arrival; the UK FCDO notes the scheme may change or extend to other airports with limited notice, so check before you fly. The FCDO also warns you may be asked to complete a health declaration, which can include proof of vaccinations. Get your passport physically stamped on arrival. Visa exemption: citizens of Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the UK, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland can stay up to 45 days from the date of entry without a visa, under a Vietnamese government resolution in force from 15 March 2025 to 14 March 2028 (extension to be considered), per the Vietnamese government news portal; the UK FCDO confirms 45 days for British citizens. E-visa: Vietnam's e-visa portal states a maximum stay of 90 days, and the FCDO and national tourism authority say multiple entry; e-visas restrict you to the entry and exit points chosen at application. Some older Vietnam tourism pages still show shorter e-visa and exemption stays (30 days, 15 to 30 days); the government portal and FCDO figures are used here. Currency: declare cash over 15 million VND or 5,000 USD (or equivalent) on arrival; to leave with more you need proof from an authorised credit institution or written State Bank of Vietnam approval (FCDO). No proof of funds, onward ticket, accommodation registration or insurance requirement is stated in the FCDO entry rules. Enter and leave on the same passport.

Hepatitis A
Hepatitis B
Typhoid
Japanese encephalitis (depending on activities and length of stay)
health.malaria_risk: Rural areas only, with rare cases in the Mekong and Red River Deltas. No transmission in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Hai Phong, Nha Trang or Quy Nhon.
health.notes: The US CDC lists no vaccination as required for entry to Vietnam, and states yellow fever vaccination is neither required nor recommended — nothing is checked at the border for a traveller arriving from a non-risk country. CDC recommends antimalarial medication for some specific provinces, and insect-bite precautions only in the Mekong and Red River Deltas. The UK FCDO notes dengue, Zika, Japanese encephalitis and malaria are all present, that many medicines sold locally are counterfeit or hard to find, and that Vietnam limits 'addictive' or 'psychotropic' medication to a 7-day supply without documentation — carry your prescription and a doctor's letter. Vietnam's national tourism authority advises bottled water and avoiding ice in rural areas, and says malaria risk is highest in the rural highlands.

money.card_acceptance: Hotels, tour operators, boutiques, restaurants, grocery stores and spas generally accept international Visa and Mastercard debit and credit cards, and Vietnam's national tourism authority says most larger travel expenses can be paid by card, on the spot or online in advance. Cash remains the norm for small purchases and street vendors.
money.cash_culture: Carry cash for street food, markets, small shops and anywhere rural — the tourism authority advises withdrawing extra before travelling to remote destinations, especially if buying crafts or textiles direct from artisans. Notes only, no coins, from 200₫ up to 500,000₫; mentally dropping three zeros makes the numbers manageable. Watch the 20,000₫ and 500,000₫ notes, which are similar shades of blue.
money.tipping: Not a normal part of Vietnamese culture and never obligatory — the tourism authority states there is no set rule. Tipping has become more common for private tour guides and in salons and spas; in restaurants and cafes it is not expected, though it is appreciated. A local meal costs roughly 30,000–40,000 VND, which is the benchmark the tourism authority suggests using to size a tip. Bargaining, by contrast, is normal in markets and casual shopping areas.
money.atm_notes: ATMs taking international cards are just outside arrivals at every major airport, and Visa is accepted at more than 20,000 ATMs nationwide. Per-transaction withdrawal limits are about 2–3 million VND at local bank ATMs and 5–10 million VND at international banks (the tourism authority's published list of higher-limit banks — ANZ, Citibank, HSBC, Commonwealth — is old enough that several of those have since scaled back retail operations in Vietnam, so treat the names, not the limits, as indicative). Conversion rates and swipe fees are set by your own card issuer. Note that buying US dollars once you are inside Vietnam is very difficult, so do not plan to reconvert.

power.frequency: 50–60Hz (as published by the US International Trade Administration; EVN publishes no figure in English)
power.adapter_note: Vietnam's national tourism authority states the supply is 220 volts and that most sockets take plugs with two round prongs (Type C); the Vietnamese Embassy in Washington also gives 220 volts. A traveller from a 230V country therefore needs only a plug adapter, not a voltage converter — and adapters are sold in any electrical shop, or lent by hotels. The tourism authority notes power cuts and surges are uncommon but do happen depending on location. Only the round-prong socket is officially described, so bring a Type C adapter rather than assuming a flat-pin plug will fit.

emergency.notes: These three numbers are published identically by Vietnam's national tourism authority and by the UK FCDO. There is no universal 112-style number: the FCDO lists 112 as national search and rescue and 111 as the child-protection hotline, not as general emergency lines. Critically, the FCDO states that emergency numbers in Vietnam are operated in Vietnamese only — if you can, have a Vietnamese speaker place the call. The FCDO also advises taking a translator when reporting a crime to police, and always obtaining a police report. No dedicated tourist-police number is published.

getting_around.summary: Vietnam is long and slow overland, and the national tourism authority openly recommends flying between distant cities — the Hanoi–Ho Chi Minh City train runs 30 hours or more (about 36 hours end to end on the Reunification Express), and central Vietnam to either end is commonly 16 hours. Domestic flights on Vietnam Airlines, VietJet and Bamboo Airways are cheap and frequent. A single 2,600 km north–south railway operated by Vietnam Railways carries five Reunification Express services a day in each direction, stopping at Hue, Da Nang, Nha Trang and Phan Thiet, with hard seat, soft seat, hard sleeper and soft sleeper classes; book days ahead normally, and two weeks ahead around Vietnamese holidays. Open-tour sleeper buses link the main tourist towns in the south and centre. Within cities, use metered taxis from the reputable operators (Vinasun and Mai Linh nationally, Taxi Group in Hanoi) or ride-hailing apps such as Grab, which require a Vietnamese SIM card to use; scooters rent for roughly 150,000–300,000 VND a day and bicycles for 20,000–30,000 VND.

connectivity.local_sim_notes: Prepaid SIM cards are sold on arrival at major airports and from shops across the country. The three GSM operators are Viettel, Vinaphone and Mobifone, all with good coverage. You must show your passport to register the SIM. A Vietnamese number is also needed to use ride-hailing apps like Grab. Wi-Fi is widespread in cafes, hotels, shops and restaurants, with free public access in several tourist hubs and major airports.
connectivity.typical_cost: Vietnam's national tourism authority lists data-only SIM cards at 100,000–200,000 VND depending on the data included, and credit top-ups in 20,000–100,000 VND increments (page checked 28 September 2026). No official figure is published for a specific 10GB / two-week bundle, and no USD equivalent is published, so treat the VND figures as the sourced ones.

climate.precipitation_note: Hanoi's 28 mm falls as grey drizzle across about 11 days rather than downpours. Ho Chi Minh City is in its dry season at 12 mm; Da Nang still catches 83 mm.
climate.crowd_note: Tet, the Lunar New Year, falls in late January or early February — the tourism authority warns most businesses and restaurants close, and transport hubs overflow in the days beforehand. Book any transport well in advance.

climate.precipitation_note: The driest stretch of the year in both ends of the country: 19 mm in Hanoi, 8 mm in Ho Chi Minh City, 22 mm in Da Nang. Northern damp lingers as low cloud more than rain.
climate.crowd_note: The other half of the Tet window. If Tet falls in February, expect widespread closures and packed buses and trains around it.

climate.precipitation_note: 55 mm in Hanoi spread over roughly 18 drizzly days — frequent, light and grey rather than heavy. The south stays dry at 18 mm.
climate.crowd_note: The tourism authority describes northern Vietnam's cold season as running December to March, so March is the tail of it — pack a layer for Hanoi and Sapa.

climate.precipitation_note: 79 mm in Hanoi. The southern wet season has not started (57 mm in Ho Chi Minh City) and Da Nang is at its driest run of the year (50 mm).
climate.crowd_note: The tourism authority calls April and May sunny with a refreshing breeze in the north, but also warns those two months can be extremely hot elsewhere — the south sits at 34–35°C highs.

climate.precipitation_note: The rains arrive at both ends: 188 mm in Hanoi and 202 mm in Ho Chi Minh City as the southwest monsoon starts. Da Nang stays comparatively dry at 71 mm.
climate.crowd_note: Heat is the main constraint — the tourism authority flags April and May as potentially extremely hot.

climate.precipitation_note: Hanoi's hottest month and thoroughly wet at 231 mm over 16 days; Ho Chi Minh City 224 mm. Afternoon downpours are the pattern rather than all-day rain.
300 mm in Hanoi across about 18 rain days, 231 mm in Ho Chi Minh City. Hot, humid and the start of the northern typhoon window.
Hanoi's wettest month at 335 mm over 18 days; Ho Chi Minh City 219 mm; rain building in Da Nang at 167 mm.
Hanoi eases to 195 mm, but central Vietnam turns sharply — Da Nang jumps to 394 mm. The tourism authority warns central Vietnam gets storms and floods in the late rainy season.
climate.crowd_note: The tourism authority names September and October as favoured months in the north for cooler temperatures and clear skies.

climate.precipitation_note: Hanoi dries out to 126 mm over about 10 days — its best balance of the year. Central Vietnam does the opposite: Da Nang records its wettest month at 658 mm over 21 days, with flooding a real risk.
climate.crowd_note: Favoured in the north for cool, clear weather per the tourism authority — but a poor month to build an itinerary around Hue and Hoi An.

climate.precipitation_note: Hanoi's dry spell begins: 48 mm over about 7 days. Ho Chi Minh City drops to 128 mm as its wet season ends. Da Nang is still very wet at 486 mm.
24 mm in Hanoi and 41 mm in Ho Chi Minh City — dry at both ends. Da Nang still takes 272 mm over 21 days.
climate.crowd_note: The north is genuinely cold by now; the tourism authority puts northern Vietnam's cold season at December to March, so bring warm clothes for Hanoi, Sapa and Ha Giang while the south stays hot and dry.
